AUTOINDEX lets Milvus pick the index type; with the default scalarAutoIndex.params.build it builds HYBRID for Int64

validation_plan: Before: on a non-production copy of default.products with production-like data, replay `price < ? and price >= ?`, `price > ?`, `price < ? and price > ?` with representative values and record p50/p95 latency without an index on price (for reference, the access log shows p50 1.630 ms, p95 14.883 ms over 20 requests).

After (baseline): on a copy with no other index on price, create index_type AUTOINDEX on field "price"; this tool does not create it. Wait until the index is built, replay the same requests, and record p50/p95 latency, build time, memory and disk use, and insert latency.
Keep the candidate with the clearest measured improvement over Before; if none improves, keep no index.

notes: Primary key: Milvus serves ==, IN and range filters on it through its built-in primary-key lookup, and this tool proposes no index for it.
Advisory only: this tool never creates, alters or drops an index.
Candidates are for validation, not changes to apply: no speedup is promised. Keep an index only if its validation plan shows a measured improvement.
AUTOINDEX is the baseline candidate wherever Milvus accepts it; a specific index type is listed only with evidence from the access log or --field-stats.
Existing indexes are listed from the snapshot; this report does not show whether any query used them.
Statistics shown as "unknown" were not provided with --field-stats; alternatives that need them are not evaluated.
Fingerprints replace every literal with ?; raw expressions, user names, client addresses and trace IDs are not reported.
